source.title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory

accepted.question_text: For a free group F_n of finite rank n >= 2 with fixed free generating set X = {x_1, ..., x_n}, suppose Y = {y_1, ..., y_n} normally generates F_n. Must Y be Andrews-Curtis equivalent to X, meaning obtainable from X by Nielsen transformations together with conjugations by elements of F_n?
For which positive integers n is every group of exponent n locally finite, with particular attention to n = 5, 8, 9, and 12?

Does every subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex remain aspherical; equivalently, if G = F/R has an aspherical presentation whose relation module R/[R,R] is a free ZG-module, must every presentation obtained by retaining only some of the relators also be aspherical?
Is the isomorphism problem solvable for arbitrary one-relator groups?
Is the conjugacy problem solvable for arbitrary one-relator groups?
Must every one-relator group that contains no Baumslag-Solitar subgroup be hyperbolic?

Let G be the direct product of two copies of the rank-n free group F_n, n >= 2, with standard generators {x_1, ..., x_n} and {y_1, ..., y_n}. Is every generating system of G with cardinality 2n Nielsen equivalent to the standard system {x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_n}?
accepted.context_brief: Direct products of free groups; source item (O7a)

accepted.question_text: Let G be the direct product of two copies of the rank-n free group F_n, n >= 2. Does every automorphism of G come from an automorphism of the ambient free group F_{2n}, that is, is every automorphism tame?
accepted.context_brief: Direct products of free groups; source item (O7b)

accepted.question_text: For nonabelian free groups, is the elementary theory of the rank-2 free group F_2 equal to the elementary theory of the rank-3 free group F_3?
For a nonabelian finite-rank free group F, is the elementary theory Th(F) decidable?
If H and K are nontrivial subgroups of a free group, must rank(H intersect K) - 1 be at most (rank(H) - 1)(rank(K) - 1)?
Is the automorphism group of a rank-2 free group linear, equivalently, is the braid group B_4 linear?
Does there exist an infinite finitely presented periodic group?
Can the integral group ring of a torsion-free group contain zero divisors?
Is there an algorithm that decides whether a given automorphism of a free group has a nontrivial fixed point?
Does the automorphism group of a free group satisfy the Tits alternative?
If an endomorphism of a finite-rank free group sends every primitive element to a primitive element, must the endomorphism be an automorphism?
For an automorphism phi of a rank-n free group F_n and an element u whose forward orbit under phi is finite, which finite orbit cardinalities can occur as u and phi vary?
Is the automorphism group of a free group rigid in the sense that it has only finitely many irreducible complex representations in each dimension?
Is the conjugacy problem solvable for the automorphism group of a finite-rank free group?
For n,k >= 2, let Epi(n,k) be the set of epimorphisms from F_n onto F_k. Do there exist two elements g_1,g_2 in F_n such that any two epimorphisms in Epi(n,k) that agree on g_1 and g_2 are equal?
accepted.context_brief: Epimorphisms of free groups; source item (F7)

accepted.question_text: Let phi be an endomorphism of a free group F_n and let S be a finite-rank subgroup of F_n. Must rank(Fix(phi) intersect S) be at most rank(S)?
In the rank-2 free group generated by x and y, is the iterated commutator [x,y,y,y,y,y,y] a product of fifth powers?
Can the commutator subgroup of a free group be defined by a first-order formula in the language of group theory?
If S is a subgroup of a free group F and R is a retract of F, must R intersect S be a retract of S?

Let F_Q be the free uniquely divisible group of rank n, and let lambda be the Magnus homomorphism from F_Q to the formal power series ring Q<<x_1,...,x_n>> induced by x_i -> 1 + x_i. Is lambda injective, equivalently, is F_Q residually torsion-free nilpotent?
Is the free uniquely divisible group F_Q linear?
accepted.context_brief: Linearity of free Q-groups; source item (F13)

accepted.question_text: Let F be a noncyclic finite-rank free group and let G be a finitely generated residually finite group. If G has the same finite homomorphic images as F, must G be isomorphic to F?
Let F be a noncyclic free group and R a noncyclic subgroup. If the commutator subgroup [R,R] is normal in F, must R itself be normal in F?

Let R be the normal closure of an element r in a free group F with its natural length function, and let s be a shortest element of R. Must s be conjugate to r, r^-1, [r,f], or [r^-1,f] for some f in F?
For a noncyclic rank-n free group F and P(n,k), the number of primitive elements of length k, what is the asymptotic growth of P(n,k) as k grows with n fixed?
For a finite-rank free group, is the c-th term of the lower central series the normal closure of the basic commutators of weight c?
Let F be a noncyclic free group and let G be the unrestricted direct product of countably many copies of F. Is the abelianization G/[G,G] torsion-free?
If an equation over a free group F has no solution in F, must there be a finite quotient of F in which the equation still has no solution?
accepted.context_brief: Equations over free groups; source item (F20)

accepted.question_text: Let G be a free product of finite-rank free groups A and B amalgamating proper subgroups H <= A and K <= B. Can G be simple?
Does the rank-2 free group have an infinite ascending chain of fully invariant subgroups, each generated as a fully invariant subgroup by one element?
Let G be the free product of two isomorphic finite-rank free groups amalgamated over a finitely generated subgroup. Is the conjugacy problem solvable in G?
Let G be the free product of two isomorphic finite-rank free groups amalgamated over a finitely generated subgroup. Is there an algorithm to decide whether G is free?
Let G be the free product of two isomorphic finite-rank free groups amalgamated over a finitely generated subgroup. Is there an algorithm to decide whether G is hyperbolic?
If two groups are equationally noetherian, meaning every finite-variable system of equations over the group is equivalent to a finite subsystem, is their free product equationally noetherian?
Are all one-relator groups with torsion residually finite?
Is the isomorphism problem solvable for one-relator groups with torsion?
For every one-relator group, is there an algorithm solving the word problem in quadratic time, or at least in polynomial time, in the input word length?
Is the generalized word problem solvable for one-relator groups, that is, can one decide whether a given group element belongs to a given finitely generated subgroup?
If the relation module of a group G is cyclic, must G be a one-relator group?
Let H = F/R be a one-relator group with R normally generated by r, and let G = F/S where S is normally generated by r^k. If H is residually finite, must G be residually finite?
Let G = F/R be a one-relator group whose relator lies in the commutator subgroup [F,F]. Must G be Hopfian?
Let G = F/R be a one-relator group whose relator lies in [F,F]. Must G be residually finite?
Let G = F/R be a one-relator group whose relator lies in [F,F]. Must G be automatic?
For a one-relator group whose relator has the commutator form [u,v], do the analogues of the Hopficity, residual finiteness, and automaticity questions from OR7 hold?
If two one-relator groups are such that one is a homomorphic image of the other, must the two groups be isomorphic?
Is every one-relator group with no nonabelian metabelian subgroup automatic?
Are all one-relator groups with torsion conjugacy separable?
Are all freely indecomposable one-relator groups with torsion co-Hopfian?
Which finitely generated one-relator groups have the property that all minimal-cardinality generating systems are Nielsen equivalent to one another?
Which finitely generated one-relator groups have only tame automorphisms, meaning automorphisms induced by automorphisms of the ambient free group?
Describe the one-relator groups that are discriminated by a free group.
If a one-relator group G has every finite-index subgroup again one-relator and every infinite-index subgroup free, must G be a surface group?
For orientable surface groups S(n) and S(m) of genera n,m >= 2, are S(n) and S(m) elementarily equivalent?
For the orientable surface group S(m), is S(m) elementarily equivalent to the free group F_{2m}?
Is the triviality problem decidable for groups given by balanced finite presentations, where the number of generators equals the number of relators?
Can a nontrivial finitely presented group be isomorphic to its direct square?
Let F_n/R = <x_1,...,x_n | r_1,...,r_m> present a nontrivial group. For any element s of the free group on x_1,...,x_n,x_{n+1}, must <x_1,...,x_n,x_{n+1} | r_1,...,r_m,s> also be nontrivial?
accepted.context_brief: Adding generators and relators; source item (FP3)

accepted.question_text: If the relation module of a group G is finitely generated, must G be finitely presented?
If a finitely presented group is trivial, can one always replace one defining relator by a primitive element without changing the group?
Must every finitely presented group have either polynomial growth or exponential growth?
accepted.context_brief: Growth of finitely presented groups; source item (FP6a)

accepted.question_text: Must every finitely presented group contain either a free semigroup on two generators or a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?
Does there exist a nonfree noncyclic finitely presented group all of whose proper subgroups are free?
Is every knot group virtually free-by-cyclic?
Is every finitely generated group discriminated by a free group finitely presented?
Is every finitely generated free-by-cyclic group finitely presented?
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?
If a relatively free group is finitely presented, must it be virtually nilpotent?
Is every finitely presented Noetherian group virtually polycyclic?
Is every residually finite Noetherian group virtually polycyclic?
Is every finitely generated perfect group G, with [G,G] = G, the normal closure of a single element?
For distinct primes p, q, and r, is the free product Z_p * Z_q * Z_r the normal closure of a single element?
Does there exist a noncyclic finitely presented group in which every element is conjugate to a power of one fixed element?
Is every countable abelian group embeddable in the center of some finitely presented group?
accepted.context_brief: Centers of finitely presented groups; source item (FP18)

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated residually finite group and phi an endomorphism of G. Must there exist k such that phi^{k+1}(G) is isomorphic to phi^k(G)?
Are all hyperbolic groups residually finite?
Does every hyperbolic group have a proper subgroup of finite index?
Are all hyperbolic groups linear?
Do hyperbolic groups with torsion have a solvable isomorphism problem?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic groups with torsion; source item (H3)

accepted.question_text: Given a finite presentation of a hyperbolic group that is not necessarily a Dehn presentation, can one find a Dehn presentation for the group in polynomial time?
Given a finite presentation of an automatic group, can one decide whether the group is hyperbolic?
Is every automatic group biautomatic?
Does every automatic group have a solvable conjugacy problem?
Is every biautomatic group that contains no subgroup isomorphic to Z x Z hyperbolic?
Can the Baumslag-Solitar group <x,y | yxy^{-1} = x^2> be embedded as a subgroup of an automatic group?
Is every retract of an automatic group automatic?
Does every hyperbolic group act properly discontinuously and cocompactly by isometries on a CAT(k) space for some k < 0?
Is every hyperbolic group equationally noetherian, meaning every finite-variable system of equations over the group is equivalent to a finite subsystem?
Is every combable group automatic?
For a fixed hyperbolic group G, is there an algorithm deciding whether a finitely generated subgroup H is malnormal, meaning that H^g intersect H is trivial for every g outside H?
If H is a finitely generated malnormal subgroup of a hyperbolic group G, must H be quasiconvex?
Is every finitely presented metabelian automatic group virtually abelian?
Does every braid group admit a faithful linear representation?
Is the Gassner representation of the pure braid group P_n faithful for every n?
Is the Burau representation of the braid group B_n faithful for n = 4 and n = 5?
Let F_n be freely generated by a_1,...,a_n. Does the equation y_1 a_1 y_1^{-1} ... y_n a_n y_n^{-1} = a_1 ... a_n have a solution with every y_i in the second commutator subgroup F_n''?
What are necessary and sufficient conditions for a square matrix over a Laurent polynomial ring to be the Burau matrix of some braid?
For n >= 4, does the braid group B_n have a nontrivial noninjective endomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Endomorphisms of braid groups; source item (B6a)

accepted.question_text: For n >= 4, is every nontrivial endomorphism of the commutator subgroup [B_n,B_n] an automorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Endomorphisms of braid groups; source item (B6b)

accepted.question_text: For n >= 4, does the braid group B_n have a proper torsion-free nonabelian factor group?
accepted.context_brief: Factor groups of braid groups; source item (B7a)

accepted.question_text: For n >= 4, does the commutator subgroup [B_n,B_n] have a proper torsion-free factor group?
accepted.context_brief: Factor groups of braid groups; source item (B7b)

accepted.question_text: For n >= 4, does every automorphism of the commutator subgroup [B_n,B_n] extend to an automorphism of B_n?
For n >= 4, does every nontrivial endomorphism of [B_n,B_n] extend to an endomorphism of B_n?
For free nilpotent groups of rank greater than 2, if an element is fixed by every automorphism of the group, must that element be the identity?
For every finitely generated nilpotent group, is its isoperimetric function equivalent to a polynomial?
Is every locally nilpotent group a homomorphic image of a torsion-free locally nilpotent group?
For a finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group G, are there only finitely many nonisomorphic groups among G, Aut(G), Aut(Aut(G)), and the subsequent iterated automorphism groups?
Is direct indecomposability decidable for finitely generated nilpotent groups?
Classify the finitely generated nilpotent groups of class 2 and genus 1, where genus 1 means that any group with the same finite homomorphic images is isomorphic to the original group.
Is the isomorphism problem solvable for finitely presented metabelian groups?
Is the automorphism group of a free metabelian group of rank greater than 3 finitely presented?
Is there an algorithm deciding whether a given finitely presented solvable group is metabelian?
Are projective groups of infinite countable rank in the class of metabelian groups necessarily free metabelian?
What can be said about the integral homology of a finitely generated metabelian group?
Does there exist a group that is not isomorphic to the outer automorphism group of any metabelian group with trivial center?
Describe the automorphism group of a finite-rank free solvable group; in particular, determine whether this automorphism group is finitely generated.
For groups with one defining relation in the variety of solvable groups of a fixed derived length, is the word problem solvable?
If a group of rank greater than 2 has one defining relation in the variety of solvable groups of a fixed derived length, must its center be trivial?

For fixed rank k and derived length d, does there exist a bound N(k,d) such that every element of the commutator subgroup of the free solvable group of rank k and derived length d is a product of at most N(k,d) commutators?
If A and B are finitely generated solvable Hopfian groups, must their direct product A x B be Hopfian?
Is the conjugacy problem solvable for finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic groups?
Does there exist a finitely presented solvable group that satisfies the maximum condition on normal subgroups and has unsolvable word problem?
Can a finitely generated free solvable group of derived length 3 be embedded in a finitely presented solvable group?

Does the rank-2 free solvable group of derived length d > 2 have any test elements, where a test element u is one whose stabilization by an endomorphism forces that endomorphism to be an automorphism?

trace.notes: Original input was the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/1421182. Local resolver metadata identified the exact work as 'Open problems in combinatorial group theory' (1999). Exact-title recovery found a readable PDF with the same title and authors Gilbert Baumslag, Alexei G. Myasnikov, and Vladimir Shpilrain.

Mapped 23-page PDF. Section hierarchy: Introduction; Outstanding Problems; Free Groups; One-Relator Groups; Finitely Presented Groups; Hyperbolic and Automatic Groups; Braid Groups; Nilpotent Groups; Metabelian Groups; Solvable Groups. Labeled problem blocks are the primary extraction regions.
Extracted 14 candidate questions from Outstanding Problems, including subquestions under O7 and O8.
Extracted 28 candidate questions from Free Groups, including subquestions under F23 and solved markers under F2 and F20.
Extracted 20 candidate questions from One-Relator Groups, including subquestions under OR7, OR13, and OR16.
Extracted 20 candidate questions from Finitely Presented Groups, including subquestions under FP6 and solved markers under FP4, FP9, FP10, and FP19.
Extracted 17 candidate questions from Hyperbolic and Automatic Groups, including subquestions under H1.
Extracted 32 candidate questions from Braid Groups, Nilpotent Groups, Metabelian Groups, and Solvable Groups, including subquestions under B6, B7, and B8.

Rewrote labeled problem statements into standalone questions by inlining local notation such as F_n, Epi(n,k), F_Q, malnormality, genus 1, and test element where the source supplied the needed context.
No near-duplicate clusters were merged; source labels identify distinct problem blocks or explicit subquestions.
Accepted rewritten items with page locators and short verbatim label anchors. Solved metadata is true only for items explicitly marked solved or explicitly resolved in the chosen source artifact.
Saved exact JSON payload to outputs/parse-paper/1421182.json and outputs/latest.json.
